page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 186.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA Turing-generation T4 GPUs with a combined 32 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage included, meaning all storage must be network-attached. Network connectivity is rated at a 15 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1104.08 and poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 35393.62 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 149.01 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is stable, averaging 1968.52 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 98.26 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Redis SET operations reach 33.17 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 22.34 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dual NVIDIA T4 GPUs makes this instance a resource-dense option for workloads that benefit from hardware acceleration without requiring the premium cost of newer-generation GPU architectures. The trade-off lies in the modest single-core CPU performance and the lack of local storage. This hardware configuration is best suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, video transcoding, parallel computing, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for parallel computing and machine learning workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it features 48 vCPUs, 186.0 GB of RAM, and two NVIDIA T4 GPUs providing a total of 32 GB of VRAM. The instance does not include local storage, relying instead on network-attached options, and delivers a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks indicate modest single-core CPU performance, but multi-core operations and memory bandwidth perform at average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 35393.62. This configuration offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU acceleration, making it highly suitable for workloads such as AI inference, video transcoding, and multi-threaded data processing where massive parallelization is required.
